subject: Day 31: blanket-on-grass window
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 31 days old. With the crying curve still climbing, a short outdoor-light and tactile window gives him novel sensory input and gives both of you a low-effort reset. Keep him in shade and keep the bout brief.

Action items
- Lay a blanket on the grass in full shade for a 10 to 15 minute outdoor window; skip direct sun, since infants under six months should be kept out of it and rely on supplementation rather than sunlight for vitamin D. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D On the Double: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Continue the 400 IU per day vitamin D drop if Avi is exclusively or predominantly breastfed; outdoor time does not replace it. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D On the Double: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Pre-schedule the 2-month visit now if it is not booked (window day 56-70); rotavirus dose one must be given by about day 104, so do not let it drift late.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Evening fussiness that resists soothing; the PURPLE crying pattern is unexpected, resistant, pain-faced, and long-lasting, and it is not a sign anything is wrong.
- [monitor] Frequent painful spit-up or refusal to feed despite hunger cues; note it and raise it at the 1-month or 2-month visit to distinguish GERD from cow's-milk-protein intolerance.
- [call within 24h] Bloody stool with mucus and blood streaks, which can point to CMPI or an anal fissure, or a sustained refusal of feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea or a color change, or a high-pitched scream with lethargy and a bulging fontanelle; this combination needs to be seen immediately to rule out meningitis!

Enrichment opportunities
- Lay Avi on a blanket on the grass in shade for a brief outdoor window; dappled light, moving air, and new textures broaden the sensory diet his developing visual and tactile systems are tuned to absorb. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D On the Double: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Bring a high-contrast black-and-white card outside and move it slowly across his field of view; he can now track objects roughly 180 degrees, so let his eyes do the work. AAP HealthyChildren: Baby ages and stages: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Run smile-and-wait turns face to face on the blanket: make an exaggerated happy face, hold it, and wait. Social smiles are consolidating this week and reward your patience. AAP HealthyChildren: Movement, Birth to 3 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 35-41 (around week 6): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit with OB clearance, mood screen, and contraception discussion.
- Day 56-70 (2-month well visit): six vaccines due, including the oral rotavirus dose that must be given by roughly day 104.
- Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): plan for 24 to 48 hours of fussiness and low-grade fever after the shots.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
